mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the monetary policy stance remains accommodative.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.0%, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 7.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through elevated corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST and RSAFS above their 50th percentiles fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 1.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days as higher discount rates reduce equity valuations and slow economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 1.0%, or the Rank IC for the tightening regime is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) above 100 indicates expanding manufacturing output, which correlates with stronger corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 100, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index exceeds 232.5, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 232.5, or the Rank IC falls below 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong labor market expansion (PAYEMS growth above 100k jobs per month), consumer spending and corporate earnings rise, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 135000, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP level (GDPC1) above 13,500 billion dollars indicates sustained economic strength, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 exceeds 13,500 billion, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year window.
